title: Professional Wireless Systems (PWS) Takes on Intercom and RF Coordination for the Biggest Rock Band on Earth
body_html:
What Was Announced

Professional Wireless Systems (PWS) has been selected to provide intercom and RF coordination services for the biggest rock band on earth, a high-profile client that has not been named. The company will handle the band's wireless communication needs, including intercom systems and RF coordination, for their upcoming tour. This decision represents a significant win for PWS, which has established itself as a leading provider of wireless solutions for the live events and broadcast industries.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The selection of PWS by the biggest rock band on earth has significant implications for the engineering and operational teams involved in the tour. By leveraging PWS's expertise in wireless communication and RF coordination, the band's crew will be able to streamline their workflow and reduce the complexity of managing multiple wireless systems. This, in turn, will enable the crew to focus on more critical aspects of the production, such as sound quality and stage management. From an operational perspective, the integration of PWS's systems will also provide a single point of control for the entire wireless infrastructure, making it easier to monitor and troubleshoot issues in real-time. The use of PWS's services also highlights the growing importance of wireless communication in live events and broadcast production. As the demand for high-quality, wireless audio continues to increase, the need for reliable and efficient wireless systems has become a top priority for production teams. By providing a comprehensive solution for intercom and RF coordination, PWS is helping to address this need and enable the delivery of high-quality audio and video content. Furthermore, the selection of PWS by the biggest rock band on earth also underscores the growing trend towards software-defined workflows in the broadcast industry. By leveraging software-based solutions, production teams can simplify their workflow and reduce the complexity of managing multiple systems. This, in turn, enables them to focus on more creative aspects of the production, such as sound design and stage management.

Industry Context

The selection of PWS by the biggest rock band on earth is part of a broader trend towards the adoption of wireless communication solutions in the live events and broadcast industries. Other companies, such as Axia and Clear-Com, have also established themselves as leading providers of wireless communication solutions for live events and broadcast production. However, PWS's expertise in RF coordination and intercom systems sets it apart from its competitors, making it an attractive choice for high-profile clients like the biggest rock band on earth. In addition, the growing demand for wireless communication solutions is also driving the development of new technologies and standards in the industry. For example, the adoption of SMPTE ST 2110, a standard for the transmission of audio and video over IP networks, is enabling the delivery of high-quality, wireless audio and video content. This, in turn, is driving the development of new wireless communication solutions that can take advantage of these emerging standards.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

The selection of PWS by the biggest rock band on earth has significant implications for broadcast and media teams involved in live events and broadcast production. Firstly, it highlights the growing importance of wireless communication solutions in the industry, and the need for production teams to invest in reliable and efficient wireless systems. Secondly, it underscores the growing trend towards software-defined workflows, and the need for production teams to simplify their workflow and reduce the complexity of managing multiple systems. From an operational perspective, the integration of PWS's systems will also provide a single point of control for the entire wireless infrastructure, making it easier to monitor and troubleshoot issues in real-time. This, in turn, will enable production teams to focus on more critical aspects of the production, such as sound quality and stage management. Overall, the selection of PWS by the biggest rock band on earth is a significant development in the live events and broadcast industries, and one that will have far-reaching implications for production teams in the years to come.
